task: Issue #123: isolate pull-request validation from trusted release infrastructure

perspectives.summary: Use GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 for PR validation, a distinct codicarium-release pool for publication, read-only PR permissions, persist-credentials=false, and document the external runner/firewall/attestation prerequisites. Do not retain a shared self-hosted fallback.

Current CI and release resolve to the same self-hosted Linux/codicarium runner group. Repository changes can separate labels and permissions, but runner ephemerality, Docker isolation, egress policy, and teardown attestations require platform provisioning and live evidence.

Untrusted PR code currently has repository-controlled shell, Docker, sudo, cache, and network execution on a mutable runner. The PR must fail closed against shared self-hosted labels, pull_request_target, secrets/write permissions, checkout credential persistence, and arbitrary release refs; do not overclaim isolation without external attestation.

Static workflow contracts, actionlint, workflow parsing, and hosted run metadata can verify repository policy. Fork canaries, runner destruction, network isolation, and cleanup attestation require platform-admin evidence; current runner inventory is empty and publication paths were not exercised.

consensus: Implement repository-enforceable trust-boundary hardening and fail-closed workflow contract tests now; track dedicated runner pools, egress/Docker isolation, and cleanup attestation as explicit external validation prerequisites rather than claiming them from static tests.
